info.name: AIMS ERP
info.description:
AIMS ERP backend — Milestone 1: Tenant Infrastructure.

The folders follow the bounded contexts of the approved architecture. Run the collection top to bottom: the Tenant Management requests store ids and codes into collection variables that later folders depend on.

Tenant resolution in this milestone uses the `x-tenant` header carrying the college's AISHE/NAAC code. That is UNAUTHENTICATED and is replaced by the authenticated strategy when auth lands — see the README.

exec: // Mint a fresh pair of college codes at the start of every run, so the
// collection can be re-run against the same database without colliding
// on the unique tenant code. 'Health' is the first request in the
// collection and therefore marks the start of a run.
const set = (k, v) => { pm.collectionVariables.set(k, v); pm.environment.set(k, v); };
// Authentication is not implemented in Milestone 1. The bearer token is
// wired up so the collection needs no restructuring once auth lands.

item.name: Update Tenant — immutable fields are ignored

request.description: Mass-assignment guard. The immutable fields are silently dropped rather than applied.
Whether the tenant's PostgreSQL schema exists, which tenant migrations it carries, and which are pending.
Applies pending tenant migrations to one college. Safe to repeat: an up-to-date tenant is a no-op.
Rolls pending tenant migrations out to every serving college, one at a time. A failure on one does not strand the rest; the response names exactly which failed.
A suspended college keeps all its data and simply stops serving requests.

item.name: Cleanup
item.description: Archives the two colleges this run provisioned. Run last. Archiving is the terminal state for a college that has served requests; it is never deleted, because its schema holds accreditation records.

request.description: Archives the college this run created, so repeated runs do not leave ACTIVE test colleges behind.
